reasons: Deviation classification is correct: p0082 defaults undesignated Materials to Type II (IBM/third-party owns all right, title and interest), and the p0085 licence back is limited to use/execute/reproduce/display/perform/distribute 'within Customer's Enterprise only' with no right to modify, prepare derivative works or sublicense — so the clause fails the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables) as well as the preferred position. This is not merely an acceptable fallback being upgraded.

Redline is actionable and directionally right: default flipped to Type I (Customer-owned) in p0082, the Type II licence broadened to perpetual with modification/derivative-works and sublicensing rights for Customer's business, and a new subsection (e) affirming Customer ownership of Content and Customer Components — matching the redline guidance (reverse direction / add licence-back / add Customer Data ownership sentence).

No assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to IBM is introduced, IBM's ownership of its pre-existing Type II Materials and Base Components is preserved, and the added ownership sentence carves out the limited rights IBM needs to perform the Services, so nothing over-reaches into new commercial terms.
Comment is accurate, in-house voice, prefixed correctly, and explains both changes and the concession that IBM may keep its platform/generic tools.

Minor, non-fatal drafting nits (the sublicence list uses 'Affiliates, Subcontractors and Services Recipients', which may not all be defined terms in this agreement, and 'paid-up' is retained rather than 'royalty-free') do not undermine the edit; they can be tidied in negotiation.
